Travis Konecny Review/Preview: As he approaches 30, can Konecny remain Flyers’ top scorer? Should he?

Charlie O'Connor
August 26, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:27
Instaread

For a season that saw Travis Konecny ultimately deliver his normal results and continue his role as the Philadelphia Flyers‘ leading scorer, Konecny’s 2025-26 campaign seemed oddly tumultuous.

That certainly wasn’t the case behind closed doors, where Konecny remained a key team leader and mentor to the team’s many young players. But as comes with the territory of being a club’s highest-paid player, outside scrutiny dogged Konecny. Konecny has always been and will always be an extremely noticeable player — both when he is playing his best, and when his production slips. From his early-season goal issues to his midseason surge to his underwhelming production in the playoffs, the spotlight rarely lacked glare when it came to Konecny.

Travis Konecny isn’t going anywhere — both his contract (lasting through 2033 and complete with a full no-movement clause) and his integral role both on and off the ice for the club ensure that. But Konecny also does turn 30 in March of 2027, and the Flyers are in the midst of a youth movement. His place as the integral piece is not guaranteed in perpetuity. He’ll need to continue to earn that role, regardless of his track record and current place of seniority, especially as the next generation of Flyers forwards (hopefully) continues to progress.

And if Konecny’s role does start to diminish a touch, it might not even be a bad thing for Konecny — and the Flyers.

Flyers make change at head athletic trainer, as Alex Ambrose takes over for Tommy Alva

Charlie O'Connor
August 10, 2026

The Philadelphia Flyers will have a new athletic trainer in 2026-27.

Multiple sources confirmed to PHLY that Tommy Alva, the team’s head athletic trainer since 2022-23, will no longer hold the position in the coming season. He will be replaced by Alex Ambrose, who has served as assistant athletic trainer with the club since 2023-24.

A team source noted that while the Flyers were happy with the job that Alva did during his four-season run as head trainer, they felt it was time to make a change and believed Ambrose was the best candidate.

Ambrose held the position of head athletic trainer for two AHL clubs — the Charlotte Checkers and Springfield Thunderbirds — prior to joining the Flyers’ organization in 2023 as assistant trainer. As for Alva — who leaves the organization in the shakeup — he had spent over a decade as an assistant trainer in the Florida Panthers organization before behind hired in 2022 by then-GM Chuck Fletcher in the wake of Jim McCrossin’s medical issues and subsequent lawsuit against the organization (along with then-assistant trainer Sal Raffa).

Now, Ambrose will take over Alva’s former position — his first time serving as head trainer of an NHL club.
